title: Parts of a Cell
seo_title: Grade 6 Cell Parts Worksheets: Organelles and Plant vs. Animal Cells
standard_text: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on parts of a cell (NGSS MS-LS1-2): nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, cell wall, chloroplasts and vacuoles, labeled cell models and plant vs. animal cells. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Each cell part has a job.
key_sub: The nucleus controls the cell, mitochondria release energy, and chloroplasts make food in plant cells.
body_html:
How to think about it

A cell is like a tiny factory. Its parts work together so the cell can live:

  • Nucleus: controls the cell's activities and holds the genetic information (DNA).
  • Cell membrane: controls what enters and leaves the cell.
  • Cytoplasm: a jelly-like fluid that holds the other parts.
  • Mitochondria: release energy from food (sugar) for the cell to use.
  • Cell wall: a stiff outer layer that supports and protects a plant cell.
  • Chloroplasts: capture sunlight to make food (sugar) by photosynthesis.
  • Vacuole: stores water and other materials.

Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria. Only plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts, and they have a large vacuole.

Example

Which part makes food in a plant cell?

Food is made using sunlight.

Answer: chloroplasts

Example

Does an animal cell have a cell wall?

Only plant cells have one.

Answer: No.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animal cells have cell walls.
  • Thinking plant cells do not have mitochondria. They do.
  • Mixing up the cell membrane (gatekeeper) and the cell wall (stiff support).

faq.q: What are the main parts of a cell?
faq.a: The nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

faq.q: How are plant and animal cells different?
faq.a: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. Animal cells do not have a cell wall or chloroplasts.
They release energy from food (sugar) so the cell can use it.
